newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco union says wants to resume talks.
newsitem.headline: Inco union says wants to resume talks.

text.p: The union representing Inco Ltd's 4,800 striking Sudbury workers said on Tuesday it has asked the provincial mediator to resume talks between the nickel giant and union leaders.

"Our committee wants to get to work and reach an agreement with the company. We have asked mediator (Dennis) Nelson to convey that message to Inco. The ball is now in their court," said Wayne Fraser, chief negotiator for the United Steelworkers of America, said in a statement.
Talks had been on hold since workers walked off the job at midnight on June 2.
The union said it asked Nelson to present the union's latest proposal regarding wages, vacation pay, contracting out and pensions to Inco's bargaining team.
Union leaders had been criticized for being out of touch with their members after workers voted June 2 to reject Inco's contract offer, which had been endorsed by union leaders.

"As a committee, we have done a lot of listening in the last couple of weeks. We believe we know what it will take to get an agreement that meets the needs of our members and gets the mines and smelter operating again in Sudbury," said Dave Campbell, president of union local 6500.
Before the strike, Inco's Ontario division was expected to produce about 230 million pounds of nickel, 200 million pounds of copper and four million pounds of cobalt in 1997.
Unionized workers at Inco's Port Colborne, Ontario refinery, which processes cobalt, precious metals and electro-nickel, on June 2 voted to accept the contract offer.
